rounds.notes:
I prefer to invest in some extra damage output early on, especially for the value it brings. At this stage, you don’t necessarily need Ability Power (AP) or survivability items—particularly since we already have Restortify available.
As long as you rotate your skills evenly, take cover as you would in a standard match, and avoid overextending, you should be in a solid position.

In Round 2, if you win and have approximately 10,000 to 15,000 gold, prioritize purchasing one Two Rare item. If you still have 1,000 to 2,000 gold remaining, spend it on any suitable Common items.

However, if you lose the round, invest in One Rare items and use any remaining gold to purchase suitable Common items.

round_upgrades.notes: This is my go-to item when facing a mirror match against another Orisa. It provides long-lasting effectiveness in prolonged fights and helps you hold your ground throughout the encounter.

This item is excellent for breaking Reinhardt’s shield before he can close the distance on your team. Forcing his barrier down early puts him on the back foot, leaving him vulnerable and effectively forcing him to wait and do nothing.

This item is highly effective in Round 2 for melting the enemy backline. However, if the enemy tank consistently stays up close and applies pressure, consider selling it by Round 3. Otherwise, if you're still getting value out of it, feel free to keep it in play.

Once you’ve equipped this item, you no longer need to worry about your weapon overheating. In fact, allowing it to overheat can trigger a faster cooldown compared to manually waiting—use this to your advantage during sustained fights.

With this item, your Energy Javelin can nearly one shot backline enemies if you manage to pin them against a wall. You'll still need to follow up with a few shots to secure the elimination, but it significantly increases your burst potential.

rounds.notes:
In Round 3, if you have over 20,000 to 25,000 gold, go ahead and purchase One Epic items along with one to two Rare items.
If you have around 18,000 to 23,000 gold, prioritize One Epic item and One Rare items. Make sure to spend all your gold—avoid leaving any unspent.

round_upgrades.notes: Only purchase this item when enemies are consistently fighting up close. Focus on maintaining headshot accuracy for maximum value. If your weapon overheats, don’t worry as long as you have Electro Light equipped, your cooldown recovery will be faster than waiting it out normally.

By Round 5, this item provides additional cooldown reduction and helps you sustain incoming damage by letting you cycle your abilities more frequently. This makes it harder for Reinhardt to land a Charge, Junker Queen to pull you with her Jagged Blade, or Ana to land a Sleep Dart or Biotic Grenade. With all that cooldown reduction, you’ll maintain pressure while denying their key abilities, making you much harder to shut down.

This item allows you to consistently generate ultimate charge by deflecting enemy abilities especially Reinhardt’s Fire Strike. The higher your Ability Power, the faster your ultimate will charge, as long as your deflect hits enemies. Try to anticipate when Reinhardt is about to throw his Fire Strike; if it’s difficult to land, draw the fight into a tight space where he’s more likely to cast. Once he does, reflect it back that’s your cue to go aggressive and lead the push.

This item Let you stay immune to CC last longer.

rounds.notes: At the final round, there isn’t much more to explain—it all comes down to team coordination and execution. Take a moment to assess the enemy’s power-ups and item builds, and adapt accordingly. To all the Orisa mains out there, I hope you’ve enjoyed experimenting with my Stadium build. Best of luck, and have fun out there.
